note: What is true about a place and not apparent from standing in it. The counterpart to placeIntel: that pays out for FAMILIARITY — what you know because you live here or keep coming back — and this pays out for LOOKING, on this visit, with a skill. Nothing here is authored per location: every entry hangs off a tag the whole city already carries or a flag the campaign has already set, so all 156 locations answer rather than the handful somebody has written up.
skillNote: The Skill is the printed id from src/data/rules/skills.json. The difficulty is a published Difficulty Value BY NAME, resolved through checkDV.getDV — so no number here was invented, and a band that stops being printed fails loudly instead of silently becoming a house rule.
factNote: `{place}` is replaced with the location's atlas name. The facts are written as something the character now knows rather than as something a narrator announces, because that is how they reach the prompt.

fromTags.fact: There is a way into {place} that is not the front door — a service way the people who run it treat as nobody's business but staff's.
{place} is not as empty as it looks. Somebody has been sleeping here, and recently.
The marks on {place} are fresh and they are not the ones you would expect — whoever is claiming this ground has claimed it lately, over somebody else's tag.
Some of what is stacked at {place} is not on any manifest. The seals do not match the paperwork on the pallets beside them.
There is a room at {place} the patients do not see, and the door to it has a better lock than the front.
What is on the shelves at {place} is not the stock. The stock is somewhere else, and somebody walks there and back.
There is a way onto the roof of {place} from the outside that does not go through the building.
{place} is watched more closely than it advertises — the cameras are not where the signs say they are.

fromFlags.fact: Somebody is taking a cut at {place}. It shows in what is missing from the shelves and in who nobody will look at.
Somebody is going through the records at {place}, and the staff know it.
The people at {place} talk in front of you now rather than around you — who has been asking after them, which night the deliveries really come, and which of the regulars is not a regular.
The room at {place} goes a half-step quieter when you come in. Nobody says anything. Nobody has to.

needsNote: `fromNeeds` is a CONCLUSION rather than a thing lying about: it is what two facts about a place add up to, so it is found with Deduction and it does not exist at all unless both of the facts it rests on exist here. Nothing declares a tag — the prerequisites do that, which is why a conclusion can never appear somewhere its evidence could not.

fromNeeds.fact: The quiet way in and the stock that is not on the paperwork are one operation: {place} is a transfer point, and somebody is timing the gap between the two.
The service way into {place} is not an oversight. The cameras are placed to leave it alone because it is covered by people instead, and people can be waited out.
The room the patients never see is why the crew claiming this ground leave {place} alone: somebody here is patching up their people, and that is the arrangement.
The cut being taken at {place} and the fresh marks outside it are the same people. Whoever is claiming this ground is the one collecting.
